<!-- agent-orchestration:issue-key=freeze-audit-20261018-easywin-demo-recordings -->

## Outcome and priority

**P2, about 2–4 hours depending on existing capture quality.** Turn the existing technical demo material into a small durable, team-accessible fallback package with verified links, version labels and a playback check. This is a focused packaging follow-up to #186, separate from implementing a live local demo (#248) and from authoring the assessed deck/report (#181/#192/#193).

## Problem and evidence

Audited Main `d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e`, 18 October 2026:

- [`r1018b-results.md`](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/docs/execution/aws/v1/evidence/r1018b-results.md) and [#186's session result](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/issues/186#issuecomment-6243593168) describe a web recording, Publisher transcript and dashboard images held outside Git in the operator's private state directory.
- No portable reviewer/team link was verified. The comment says the scaling/pipeline screen recordings were not made; logs/receipts do exist.
- Web time-to-player was about 134.8 seconds; the three-clip Publisher run took 272 seconds. Replaying everything serially without planning consumes a large part of the demo segment.
- A fresh full cloud deployment takes roughly 25 minutes. It is unsuitable as an operation the audience must wait for during the presentation.
- #248 establishes that the advertised local interactive fallback needs technical work; keep the recording fallback independent of that change.

The audit did not inspect private capture contents or test sharing permissions. Verify them before saying the package is ready.

## Suggested package

Use the already chosen team-accessible storage channel. Keep large video outside Git and add a small technical index containing:

1. Short labelled web register/sign-in/upload/status/playback capture.
2. CLI publishing/result capture or a readable transcript with the published client version.
3. Scaling result figure/receipt and the corresponding pipeline run links or capture.
4. A failure/retry/restore segment only to the extent it was actually recorded/proven; retain the distinction between operator restore and the cancelled deliberate CD rollback.
5. Environment, source SHA, capture date, relevant image/config identities and whether each segment is recorded or live. A V1 recording must not be relabelled as current V2 proof.
6. Playback instructions, duration and a local offline copy or equivalent backup for the presenting machine.

Trim waits without falsifying elapsed times or hiding failures; use a clearly indicated cut/time annotation if necessary. Do not invent a missing capture, target result or footage. Request access to existing private files through the established owner process rather than copying a whole deployment-state directory.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Package includes a viewable web/CLI fallback plus traceable scaling and pipeline evidence, or an explicit list of unavailable segments.
- [ ] Each segment has correct source/environment/date labels and a link to the supporting retained receipt/run.
- [ ] The package has a durable team/reviewer access path and a documented local presentation backup; developer-home paths alone are insufficient.
- [ ] A second team member opens the links and plays the recording with sound/appropriate video quality; retain the check result and date.
- [ ] Duration is practical for the existing presentation plan and includes a clear way to recover if the live path is slow or unavailable.
- [ ] Recorded versus live, edited waits, failed attempts and unproven steps are identified honestly.
- [ ] Capture/index contains no credentials, cookies, signed URLs or private operator-state contents.
- [ ] Technical package links are ready for later consumption by #192/#193 without drafting those assessed artifacts or changing the roadmap's design.

Related: #179, #186, #192, #193, #248 and the evidence-retention/results-summary tickets. This issue does not authorize a new cloud deploy, a fresh long benchmark, an upload to an arbitrary new service or sending recordings to others.

<!-- agent-orchestration:note-key=freeze-audit-20261018-easywin-coordination -->

## Agent coordination

Full handoff: #258. Consume retained proof from #250 and the scoped results figure from #252; feed verified capture identities/links into #255. The recording fallback can be packaged independently of the interactive launcher fix #248.

## Outcome and priority

**P2, roughly 15–30 minutes per member/owner with course access.** Resolve the small external-information gaps that can invalidate an otherwise ready submission: current upload cutoffs, progress-report receipt, individual peer-assessment instructions and final submission access. Record verified facts and references; this is not deck/report authoring and does not lift #181's hold.

## Known source facts and unknowns

The 18 October audit read the supplied original course documents and recorded team decisions:

- Team 17 presentation: **26 October 2026, 14:35–15:15 Singapore**. The allocated 40 minutes include Q&A. The supplied guidelines do not require a 40-minute talk or a separate official code-freeze date.
- Final report: **16 November**, incorporating presentation feedback.
- Exact upload times, separate slide/code cutoffs, latest Canvas changes and current individual peer-assessment deadline were not independently verified by the repository audit.
- The briefing requires individual peer assessment with unique ranks; its submission is distinct from uploading the group report. Do not infer completion from group participation.
- [`project-roadmap/records/project-decisions.txt:83–92`](https://github.com/Collaboration95/dc2/blob/d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e/project-roadmap/records/project-decisions.txt#L83) records the user's explicit override: the first and **only** progress report is due **16 October**; no additional weekly deadlines/recurrences are authorized. Verify that receipt rather than creating a new reporting schedule from older fortnightly wording in #191.
- #191 already owns actual member hours/milestones. The proposal's 31 person-days, commit counts and agent elapsed hours are not measured member effort.

Main baseline: `d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e`. Original sources are under `project-documentation/original-reference/`; preserve those files.

## Checklist for the course-access owner

1. Check current Canvas/NUS email instructions and record official date, time, timezone, destination and who uploads for the group. Keep internal team targets labelled as internal.
2. Confirm any separate presentation slides, code/archive, video or link-sharing requirements, allowed file types and access conditions.
3. Confirm the 16 October progress report was submitted; retain its reference/status or explicitly record a missing/unknown receipt and the actual next action.
4. Each member checks their own peer-assessment form/deadline and submits as required. Retain confirmation privately; public project tracking needs only a completion/reference status, not individual ranks or assessment content.
5. Check that the final source reference, pipeline/test scripts, report, evidence and recording links can be opened by the intended assessor/team account.
6. Identify the owner who retains final upload confirmation, and the buffer/check for upload problems. Do not invent a course cutoff from a proposed team schedule.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A small checklist records verified official presentation/report and any separate code/slides/video cutoffs with source/date/timezone, or explicitly marks unresolved facts Unknown.
- [ ] Internal team dates are not presented as course mandates; no official code-freeze date is invented.
- [ ] The single required progress-report receipt/status is verified against the recorded override; no unauthorized recurrence or extra report is created.
- [ ] All three members have an explicit individual peer-assessment completion/owner check and the actual deadline is recorded from the course channel.
- [ ] Required package contents, allowed format and assessor link-access requirements are known before the final upload.
- [ ] Final uploader/receipt owner and a practical pre-deadline access/upload check are assigned from real member input.
- [ ] Public tracking excludes personal assessment content and private course-account material.
- [ ] This task does not fabricate hours, draft held deck/report content, send messages to others, or change official source documents.

Related: #181, #191, #192, #193 and the release-manifest/demo-package tickets. A human or connected session with the relevant course access supplies external facts; repository evidence alone cannot establish them. No new security infrastructure, cloud deployment or schedule automation is part of this task.

<!-- agent-orchestration:note-key=freeze-audit-20261018-easywin-coordination -->

## Agent coordination

Full handoff: #258. Use #191 for actual member hours/progress-report ownership and #255/#254 for package/link checks. Verify the external course facts with the responsible member; the #181 assessed-authoring hold is unchanged.

<!-- agent-orchestration:issue-key=freeze-audit-20261018-easywin-handoff-index -->

## Purpose

One entry point for the fixing agent: the **six bug handoffs and nine remaining easy-win handoffs** from the 18 October code-freeze/submission audit. The user requested these issue write-ups so another agent can carry out the work. This index organizes the existing tickets; it does not duplicate their implementation, approve cloud operations or lift the assessed-authoring hold in #181.

Audit baseline: Main `d2070db68c6b3545881eb948046b8e57f47e078e`. Local audit `7ee3de5` has the same runtime tree. Re-read current source, issue/PR state, AGENTS.md and `docs/project2-worklog.txt` before implementing. Each child handoff contains its own evidence, scope, estimated effort, validation and acceptance criteria.

## Bugs already written up

- [x] **#243 — P1:** account switching exposes previous-owner Library/Admin state and captured playback capabilities. Applies to V1 and V2; repair and regressions first.
- [x] **#244 — P1 for V2-live:** direct Processing API retry/cancel bypasses idle-marker wiring and can stall repair. Includes code, IAM/environment and quiet-start regression requirements.
- [x] **#245 — P2:** Publisher quick-start/help uses `/api` instead of `/api/media`. Also document bounded cloud wait budgets and resuming status with the accepted job ID.
- [x] **#246 — P2:** Library/Admin failures are shown as successful empty results.
- [x] **#247 — P2:** clean-clone bootstrap omits pinned Moto and the Chromium required by V1.
- [x] **#248 — P2 / conditional demo blocker:** supply an honest interactive web+worker handoff; `v1-serve` is currently API-only.

## Remaining easy wins

- [x] **#249 — Current documentation and links:** reconcile V1/V2 status, successful r1019a proof, shared code/limitations, operator/workflow guidance and broken source/draft pointers.
- [x] **#250 — Evidence preservation:** archive redacted successful receipts with source/hash attribution and retain future critical artifacts through submission/review. Handle current expiry independently of future retention settings.
- [ ] **#251 — Optional P3 CI:** scan the exact already-built V1 Media, Processing and worker artifacts; preserve identity and existing gate policies without redundant builds.
- [x] **#252 — Results summary:** publish concise actual-versus-target data/table/figure with workload, environment, timing boundary, misses and missing measurements stated accurately.
- [ ] **#253 — Project/epic reconciliation:** reuse Project 14, repair stale Workflow/checklists, add native relationships and real ownership, and avoid duplicate accepted implementation.
- [ ] **#254 — Portable demo recordings:** package and verify durable web/CLI/pipeline/scaling evidence and a usable presentation-machine fallback.
- [ ] **#255 — Release manifest:** prepare the sanitized source/image/schema/config/fixture/evidence manifest and populate/accept it for the final verified release.
- [x] **#256 — Recovery-bound clarity:** document and locally exercise failed marker write → healthy stale read → delayed repair/sweep; keep this distinct from #244 and from unproven AWS timing claims.
- [ ] **#257 — Course submission checks:** verify current official cutoffs, the single progress-report receipt, individual peer assessment and final package/link access with the relevant course-access owner.

## Execution order and grouping

1. **Fix the behavior blockers:** #243, and #244 if the selected release uses V2-live. They are reproducible local defects. Targeted regressions must demonstrate the repaired behavior; an old green full suite is not enough.
2. **Preserve existing proof immediately in parallel:** #250 is time-sensitive because the examined 18 October artifacts expire around 1 November, before the 16 November report. No rerun of a successful cloud deploy is needed for retention.
3. **Complete the small client/local-demo work:** #245/#246/#247/#248, with the frontend and bootstrap coordination below. Use existing frontend/engine/harnesses; avoid new architecture.
4. **Consolidate the story and evidence:** #249/#252/#254/#256. #257 needs real course/member information; begin obtaining those facts without pretending agent time or old repo notes establish them.
5. **Make tracking useful:** #253 re-reads live state after these issues exist and includes this index and the current bug/easy-win cards. Preserve historical and not-planned items.
6. **Accept the final release identity:** #255 can be prepared earlier but only finalized against the integrated tested candidate and applicable proof. Keep immutable `project2-v1` intact.
7. **Fit optional CI work around stabilization:** #251 is useful but is not a new mandatory course requirement or reason to hold an otherwise accepted V1 indefinitely.

If delegating, group several related issues per agent rather than one agent per tiny task. One practical bundle is #243–#248 for runtime/client/demo stabilization, and another is the documentation/evidence/CI/tracking close-out (#249–#256), with the human course checks in #257. Serialize edits to shared files and mutable live work; this is an execution suggestion, not a request to launch agents now.

## Shared-file and dependency coordination

- **#243 and #246:** both edit `frontend/app.js` list loaders. Apply session/privacy fencing first or combine the changes; retaining stale data must never expose another owner.
- **#247 and #248:** clean-checkout interactive acceptance depends on the prerequisite recipe. They share README/local-runtime instructions; reuse existing setup and work-pump support.
- **#249/#250/#252/#256:** one coordinator should own overlapping `docs/evidence-index.md`/runbook/status edits and combine the final coherent wording.
- **#250 and #251:** artifact-retention and V1 scanning may touch the same workflows. Coordinate their CI changes, preserving selective lane behavior and current release/secret-scan gates.
- **#244 and #256:** fix missing writer registration independently from the pre-existing best-effort-marker failure contract. Do not claim the former proves an unconditional two-minute recovery guarantee.
- **#255:** consumes final identities, required verification, retained evidence and demo package; an incomplete draft is not an accepted release freeze.

## Work already tracked elsewhere; do not duplicate it

- **#229:** outstanding retained AWS security-negative acceptance. A merged harness or a generic smoke is not its completion.
- **#238** under **#234–#237:** the selected V2-live in-place update/release/scaling/pause/idle-cost checklist. Basic deploy/smoke has succeeded; this does not establish every acceptance row.
- **#186** under **#179:** residual cloud-proof/recording/billing disposition, including unmeasured lost-message timing, duplicate outputs and deliberate CD rollback. Narrow handoffs above support its close-out; they do not silently close it.
- **#181/#191/#192/#193:** actual member effort, deck/demo script/rehearsal and final report. Their existing explicit human authoring hold remains. Gathering technical evidence and verified facts does not invent hours or start the held artifacts.
- **#68/#80:** optional experiments; **#93/#94** remain parked/not planned. More services, physical DB splitting, Kubernetes and a new identity/security platform are outside this close-out.

## Completion discipline

Link each implementation PR and exact-source verification to its issue. Reconcile merged code separately from local runtime acceptance and real AWS evidence. Preserve historical FAILs, NOT_RUNs, timing boundaries and observed workload limitations. A target miss can be an honestly accepted result; it is not automatically permission for another optimization programme.

The user's current request is to create these issue handoffs. Application code, cloud resources and Project metadata were not changed by writing them. The fixing agent must follow current repository/user authorization for implementation, merge and any live operations. All GitHub access uses authenticated `gh` exclusively.
